claims.text: In single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys, increasing atomic size mismatch among constituent elements enhances local lattice distortion.
Enhanced local lattice distortions pin dislocations more effectively.
More effective dislocation pinning increases the barrier to dislocation motion.
The increased barrier to dislocation motion raises hardness and yield strength through solid-solution strengthening.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can serve as a single-phase FCC baseline alloy.
The proposed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi baseline has minimal atomic size mismatch.
Arc melting, homogenization, and solution annealing can produce a uniform baseline microstructure in the proposed alloy.
Substituting one or two elements with elements of substantially different atomic radii can systematically vary atomic size mismatch while retaining a similar electron concentration.
X-ray line broadening or EXAFS can quantify the relevant local lattice distortions.
Alloys with greater atomic size mismatch will exhibit higher hardness than the baseline alloy.
Alloys with greater atomic size mismatch will exhibit higher yield strength than the baseline alloy.
Hardness increase will correlate approximately linearly with lattice-distortion magnitude measured by X-ray line broadening or EXAFS.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold when electron concentration is constant, the alloys remain single-phase, processing is uniform, and testing is quasi-static at room temperature.
Formation of secondary phases may cause deviations from the proposed size-mismatch strengthening relationship.
Thermal activation at higher temperatures may alter dislocation dynamics and cause deviations from the proposed relationship.
Changes in bonding character or ordering caused by substitution may also affect hardness and strength.
The relationship between lattice distortion and hardness may become nonlinear at very high atomic misfit.
